items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: And Bob Wilber who was here before — I mean all of them. They have tremendous talent. Look at Wilber. He writes and he directs and he plays and he arranges and he’s got a hell of a talent.

ctx.x: Did you have aspirations to do music full time?

No. I do now but I didn’t. I look at the fellas that I admire so, and I think God what I wouldn’t give to have that talent. Because it’s God given, the good ones. They don’t learn it, you can’t learn it. You either got it or you don’t got it. And I look at like Kenny Davern who is coming up here today, his talent on clarinet is unmatched. And where did it come from? He didn’t do it learning scales. I don’t know whether he got it from Pee Wee Russell or where, but he’s a very instinctive player. And Bob Wilber who…
